# Behavioral Specification: SRAM Read/Write Arbiter for Mailbox Memory Access

## 1. Overview

This module arbitrates and performs single-word, 32-bit read and write accesses to a memory system on behalf of two mailbox clients:

- An inbound mailbox client that writes data to memory.
- An outbound mailbox client that reads data from memory.

The module is responsible for:

- Accepting read and write requests from the two clients.
- Arbitrating between simultaneous requests.
- Issuing one memory transaction per accepted request.
- Limiting the number of outstanding memory transactions.
- Forwarding read responses to the outbound client.
- Reporting completion of all outstanding traffic.
- Reacting to an abort acknowledgement from the host side.
- Reporting memory errors and data-integrity errors.

The address path is 32 bits wide and the data path is 32 bits wide. The memory port follows the TL-UL protocol.

## 2. Reset and Idle Behavior

On reset, the module shall:

- Have no outstanding memory transactions.
- Not assert any request grants.
- Not assert read-response-valid.
- Assert the all-transfers-complete indication whenever no client is requesting access.

After reset, the module shall be ready to accept requests from either client.

## 3. Request Acceptance

The inbound write client presents a write request together with a write address and write data. The outbound read client presents a read request together with a read address.

A request is accepted only when the client asserts its request and the module asserts the corresponding grant in the same cycle. If no grant is asserted, no memory transaction is issued and the request remains pending and may be accepted in a later cycle.

The module shall not assert a grant when no request is being presented.

## 4. Arbitration Between Read and Write Requests

If a read request and a write request are presented at the same time, the module shall prioritize the read request. A read request may be granted before a write request that arrived in the same cycle.

A write request shall be granted only when no read request is currently being presented. The module is not required to provide any fairness guarantee; read requests always take priority.

## 5. Memory Transaction Behavior

Each accepted request shall cause exactly one 32-bit memory access.

- For a read request, the module shall perform a read from the supplied read address.
- For a write request, the module shall perform a write of the supplied write data to the supplied write address.
- A write shall access the full 32-bit word; all byte lanes shall be active.
- The module shall not modify or offset the supplied addresses.
- The module shall not modify the write data.

The module shall include the integrity information required by the memory protocol for write transactions. For read transactions, the module shall check the integrity of the returned data and report a data-integrity error if the check fails.

## 6. Outstanding Transaction Limit

The module shall support up to four outstanding memory transactions.

A transaction is outstanding from the cycle it is accepted until the memory system returns a response for it.

When four transactions are outstanding, the module shall not accept any new request and shall not assert any new grant. Requests presented while the limit is reached shall remain pending. Once a response completes and capacity becomes available, the module may accept pending requests again.

The module shall handle the case where a memory response arrives in the same cycle as a new request is accepted, without losing the response and without allowing more than four outstanding transactions.

## 7. Read Response Behavior

The module shall provide a read-response-valid indication to the outbound read client.

This indication shall be asserted only for data-bearing read responses from the memory system. It shall not be asserted for write-completion responses.

When read-response-valid is asserted, the read data output shall carry the data word returned by the memory system for the corresponding read. When read-response-valid is deasserted, the read data output shall not be considered valid.

A memory response that arrives when the module is not tracking any outstanding request shall be ignored and shall not cause read-response-valid to be asserted.

## 8. Completion Indication

The module shall provide a global all-transfers-complete output.

This output shall be asserted when:

- No inbound write request is currently being presented.
- No outbound read request is currently being presented.
- No previously accepted memory transaction is outstanding.

The output shall be deasserted whenever any request is being presented or any outstanding transaction remains.

This indication is global: it does not distinguish between read completions and write completions.

## 9. Abort Handling

The module receives an abort acknowledgement from the host side. This input indicates that an abort operation has been acknowledged.

When the abort acknowledgement is asserted, the module shall:

- Clear all tracking of outstanding memory transactions.
- Treat all previously outstanding transactions as no longer outstanding for the purpose of completion reporting.
- If a response arrives after the abort when no request is tracked or accepted in the same cycle, suppress read-response-valid and leave the outstanding-transaction count unchanged.

After the abort has been acknowledged, new requests shall be accepted and tracked normally. Their responses shall be forwarded according to the normal read-response behavior.

The module itself does not initiate an abort; it only reacts to the host-side abort acknowledgement.

## 10. Error Reporting

The module shall provide two error outputs:

- A memory error output, asserted when a memory response indicates an error status.
- A data-integrity error output, asserted when a memory response fails data-integrity checking.

These error outputs shall reflect the status of memory responses. They are not masked merely because a response is ignored for read-data forwarding or because it arrives after an abort. If the memory system reports an error on a response, the module shall report that error.

The module shall not assert error outputs except in response to a memory response status or a detected data-integrity failure.
